title: Midterm Eve: Final Polls, a Closing Pitch, and a Texas Senate Race to Watch

content:
One day before the 2026 midterm elections, the final national polls point to a competitive finish — and a closing pitch from President Donald Trump, who is scheduled to speak at the Reflecting Pool in Washington on Monday afternoon after a weekend of last-minute campaign stops.

A final set of New York Times/Siena University polls finds Democrats leading their Republican rivals in five of seven contested states that will determine control of the Senate, and within the margin of error in two others, according to USA Today's live election coverage.

In Texas, the same polling finds Democratic state Rep. James Talarico at 50% to Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton's 43% in the U.S. Senate race — a contest Texas voters will decide Tuesday. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton leads Republican Sen. Roger Marshall 49% to 44%, and in Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers 53% to 42%.

Michigan's race was shaken over the weekend when El-Sayed's former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, endorsed Rogers, prompting a staff exodus from her camp, according to Fox News' live coverage. In Alaska, a federal judge dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit seeking to block certification of that state's Senate results.

The same coverage reports that Sen. Chris Murphy suffered a minor stroke Sunday while watching his son's hockey game and is recovering at Johns Hopkins. And with all 435 House races on the ballot, Republicans defending a slim 218-214 majority, political experts project Democrats are likely to win control of the chamber, USA Today reports.

For Webb County readers, the national picture lands close to home: the Texas Senate race and the TX-28 House contest are on Tuesday's ballot here, alongside Laredo's mayoral and council races. The Times' final national poll also puts the president's approval at 36%, with 61% disapproving — the lowest for any president heading into a midterm in 80 years, according to the poll tracker.
